summary: DIAGNOSIS ONLY — Duplicate startup app icon in Chrome Incognito. Reproduced deterministically in a fresh Playwright context (incognito-equivalent) with the /api/notes endpoint stubbed to return []. During app startup there is a ~1300ms window (t≈2315ms → t≈3705ms after navigation, in our measurements) where TWO rabbits are simultaneously in the DOM: (1) the inline boot splash rabbit rendered by index.html (#ir-boot-splash > img.ir-splash-rabbit, 200x200 centered, fades out 1400ms after DOMContentLoaded over 380ms + 500ms removeChild), and (2) the React empty-state rabbit inside NotesApp.jsx renderNotes() when processedNotes.length === 0. VERDICT ON WHICH EMPTY-STATE: the SECOND rabbit is the DEFAULT empty-state (data-testid="empty-state-rabbit" at NotesApp.jsx:2672-2678), NOT the uncategorized-empty-state (data-testid="uncategorized-empty-state" at NotesApp.jsx:2646-2660). The default branch fires because filterBy defaults to 'all' and searchQuery is empty at initial mount; the uncategorized branch would only fire if the user explicitly selects the Uncategorized filter. No code changes made — pure diagnosis as instructed.
verdict: CONFIRMED — duplicate rabbit is #ir-boot-splash .ir-splash-rabbit (index.html:162) overlapping [data-testid='empty-state-rabbit'] (NotesApp.jsx:2673). The 'empty-state-rabbit' (default branch), not 'uncategorized-empty-state', is what renders behind the splash.

reproduction_recipe.browser_context: Fresh browser context (Playwright browser.new_context() ≈ Chrome Incognito) — no SW cache, no IDB, no localStorage.
reproduction_recipe.network_condition: /api/notes** stubbed to return [] (simulates first-time user with no server data OR slow/offline network before hydration).
reproduction_recipe.trigger: Any navigation that leaves processedNotes.length === 0 while the boot splash is still visible (splash hides ~1400ms after DOMContentLoaded, fades over 380ms + 500ms unmount).
reproduction_recipe.not_reproducible_when: Backend seed contains notes (current preview has 7 restored notes) OR IDB/localForage already contains prior notes — in that case processedNotes hydrates non-empty before the splash fades and only the splash rabbit is ever visible.

storage_state.note: Chrome Incognito does register the SW and create the IronRabbit IDB db within the incognito session (it just doesn't persist across sessions). This matches the observed behavior.

root_cause: Two independent sources render the same /icon-192.png at startup: (a) the inline HTML boot splash in /app/frontend/public/index.html:160-164 (fixed, z-index 9999, hides 1400ms after DOMContentLoaded with a 380ms opacity transition and 500ms delayed removeChild — total lifetime ~2280ms after DCL); and (b) the React empty-state fallback in /app/frontend/src/NotesApp.jsx:2672-2678 which mounts synchronously on the first paint of NotesApp when processedNotes is []. When notes hydrate quickly (from IDB restore or a fast /api/notes response) the empty state never renders and there is no duplicate. In a real Chrome Incognito first-visit with no local data, the empty state renders while the splash is still fading, producing the reported 'two rabbits'.

which_empty_state_verdict.lines: 2672-2678 (inside renderNotes(), the default/else branch, wrapped by 'if (processedNotes.length === 0)' at line 2638)
which_empty_state_verdict.not: data-testid='uncategorized-empty-state' at lines 2646-2660 — that branch only fires when filterBy==='uncategorized' && !searchQuery, but the app's initial filterBy is 'all'

recommendation_for_main_agent_not_applie: Hide/skip the empty-state rabbit while #ir-boot-splash is still in the DOM (e.g., check document.getElementById('ir-boot-splash') === null before rendering the empty-state ), OR
Delay React's initial 'empty' render by keeping a 'hydrating' state true until first notes load attempt resolves (even if it resolves to []), OR
Have the splash listen for a 'ir-app-ready' event dispatched by NotesApp after initial hydration and hide immediately when that fires (avoids the fixed 1400ms timer window entirely).
Any of the three would eliminate the ~1.3s duplicate-rabbit window without changing branding.

ui_bugs.issue: Two rabbit icons visible simultaneously for ~1300ms in Chrome Incognito first-visit when server has no notes for the user
ui_bugs.priority: MEDIUM (cosmetic startup glitch, only affects fresh incognito / new users / offline first-load)

action_items: DIAGNOSIS ONLY — no fixes applied per user instruction.
If main agent chooses to fix: gate the empty-state rabbit render on splash absence (see recommendation_for_main_agent_not_applied).
critical_code_review_comments: The boot splash uses a fixed 1400ms timer for hide + 380ms fade + 500ms unmount, totaling ~2280ms of splash lifetime after DOMContentLoaded. This is independent of actual React hydration/data-load state, so on fast networks the splash lingers past app ready; on slow networks it can disappear before content is ready. A ready-event handshake would be more robust.

renderNotes() has no 'hydrating/loading' guard — it goes straight from mount to 'empty state' on the first render tick when processedNotes is []. Adding an isHydrating flag (true until IDB restore + first API resolution completes) would prevent flashes of empty state for users who DO have notes but experience slow hydration.
Both empty-state branches use the same pattern — could be extracted into a small component to avoid duplication and centralize the splash-visible guard.

success_rate.frontend: 100% — duplicate reproduced + specific empty-state identified as instructed

seed_data_creation: None — used stubbed /api/notes → [] via Playwright route interception; no test data written to backend.
context_for_next_testing_agent: To reproduce the duplicate rabbit: (1) create a fresh Playwright context via browser.new_context(), (2) route('**/api/notes**', respond 200 []), (3) navigate to preview root, (4) poll DOM every 100ms and check querySelectorAll('img[src*="icon-192"]').length — it will be 2 for ~1300ms in the window ~t+2300ms to ~t+3700ms. The 2nd rabbit is [data-testid='empty-state-rabbit'] from NotesApp.jsx:2673, NOT [data-testid='uncategorized-empty-state'] (that requires filterBy='uncategorized' which is not the default). Preview currently has 7 seeded notes so without stubbing the notes API you will NEVER see the duplicate — the server-restored notes hydrate before the splash fades.
rca_of_the_issue: Two independent /icon-192.png nodes co-exist in the DOM during a ~1.3s startup window in Chrome Incognito (or any fresh no-data first-load): the fixed-timer boot splash in public/index.html and the React empty-state fallback in NotesApp.jsx renderNotes()'s default branch. Mitigation: gate the React empty-state render on the boot splash being absent, or replace the splash's fixed 1400ms timer with a 'ir-app-ready' event dispatched by NotesApp after first-hydration completes.
